Red List Authority Coordinator: Roslaind Kennedy (email: Rosalind.Kennerley@durrell.org)

documentation.range: This species is found in the eastern foothills of the Andes to west of the lower Rio Negro, north of the Amazon in Southern Venezuela, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru, and south of the Amazon river in Peru, Bolivia, and Brazil to at least the Rio Madeira. Elevation from Amazon Basin at 50 m to 1,200 m on the Andean Slopes (Gilbert 2016, Patton and Emmons 2015).
documentation.population: There is no information on population numbers for this species.
documentation.habitats: This terrestrial species occurs in lowland evergreen tropical forest (Eisenberg and Redford 1999). It can exist in altered areas close to natural forest. It scatters and hoards the fruits and nuts it consumes (Patton and Emmons 2015). Captive studies suggest the species could be monogamous (Eisenberg and Redford 1999). Gestation is 99 days after which a litter, usually of two, is produced (Eisenberg and Redford 1999).
documentation.threats: The major threats to this species have not been confirmed but M. acouchy is over-hunted within its range. Also, M. acouchy is kept as a pet in some indigenous populations in Brazil, this is probably the case for M. pratti too.
documentation.measures: There is no information on the conservation status of this species.
documentation.rationale: This species is listed as Least Concern because of its wide distribution, presumed large population, occurrence in a number of protected areas, tolerance to some degree of habitat modification, and because it is unlikely to be declining at nearly the rate required to qualify for listing in a threatened category.
documentation.taxonomic_notes: Considerable variation in color and mensural characteristics exist over the range of this species, suggesting that M. pratti may be a complex of closely related taxa worthy of recognition at the species level.  Further character analyses within coherent geographic units are required to determine the validity of recognizing multiple species within M. pratti.
